item.title: Security and Derivative Pricing with Fast Regime Switches
item.description: arXiv:2611.00466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A regime-switching model lets any parameter of a standard model take a different value in each state of a hidden Markov chain. For the affine and exponential-L\'evy models in common use the pricing problem reduces to one linear system, a' = (Q + diag g(t)) a, with the chain's generator Q and a model-specific forcing g as its only ingredients. We expand its solution in the mean holding time of the chain to any order, with an initial layer for the starting regime, and identify the first correction as a Green-Kubo matrix from the group inverse of Q. The same system prices bonds, swaptions, caps, credit default swaps, Asian and digital options, and equity options under stochastic rates, with the Gil-Pelaez integrals conditioned on the regime at expiry where a payoff depends on it; barrier, American and Bermudan instruments go to the coupled equations on a grid. Every numerical claim is checked against QuantLib in the limit where the regimes coincide and against an independent referee with switching on, and the implementation is public.
item.dc:creator: Peter Cotton

item.title: Non-Convex Market Makers: Coherence without Convexity, Friction, and Parallel Composition
item.description: arXiv:2611.00502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cost-function market makers are always assumed convex, and convexity is not what makes them coherent. For a path-independent maker the exact no-arbitrage condition is a chord condition, that every chord slope of the cost lie in the convex hull of payoffs; convexity enters the standard axiomatics through a separate requirement, monotone information incorporation, and dropping it leaves coherent non-convex makers. Rational flow against such a maker trades the convex envelope, so non-convexity costs expressiveness rather than soundness, and a proportional fee of at least the arbitrage depth restores no-arbitrage, which by conjugation is a bid-ask spread with an exact no-trade interval for any cost whatever. Combining fee-bearing makers is an infimal convolution solved by one monotone clearing-price root-find, with sparse participation and a consolidated limit order book as the aggregate, and a deep quadratic co-quoter is Moreau smoothing, which preserves coherence at every depth. Any quoted configuration outside the coherent hull admits a portfolio priced below its worst payoff, so arbitrageurs act as decentralized separation oracles, and coherence is relative to friction and to the cost of finding certificates.
item.dc:creator: Peter Cotton

item.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and It\^o calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix. The notes are open source: the LaTeX source is available at https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-financial-derivatives, and readers are invited to submit corrections and additions.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Lorig

item.title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00578v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension. In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(\lambda^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ding, Sotirios Sabanis, Ying Zhang

item.title: Consumption and Investment with Multiple Job-Switching Opportunities
item.description: arXiv:2611.00900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-horizon optimal switching with affine rewards in a consumption-investment model with finitely many occupational regimes. Directed shortest-path costs yield the exact natural borrowing limit. A dual transformation reduces the control problem to a one-dimensional system of variational inequalities with interconnected obstacles. Convexity and a distributional waiting inequality give local spatial $C^{1,1}$ regularity and smooth fit, including destination ties. These estimates establish strong duality and recover optimal consumption, investment, and switching strategies. A reflected backward stochastic differential equation representation yields a set-based integral formula without prescribed boundary geometry. Every connected component of the spatially regular locus is a maximal smooth graph over time. Exact examples exhibit disconnected contact sets, temporal boundaries under strict triangle costs, and a corner in an individual boundary component under additive route costs. A convergent time discretisation completes the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon

item.title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
item.description: arXiv:2611.01892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Goluba Yurieva

item.title: Optimal Annuitization, Consumption, and Investment with Costly Capital Injections
item.description: arXiv:2611.02558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a joint optimal decision of portfolio, consumption, and annuitization for a pension-plan manager who balances retirement consumption benefits against the cost of maintaining the solvency of pension account. The pension sponsor provides costly capital injection to prevent negative wealth. Annuity purchases are irreversible, and injected funds remain in the liquid account and earn interest. Using the Legendre transform, we derive a semi-explicit solution to the associated free-boundary problem and verify the optimality of the resulting strategies. We identify an endogenous annuity-income threshold separating injection-active and injection-inactive regions and characterize six policy regimes arising from the interplay between capital injections and consumption constraints. Compared with the no-injection benchmark, capital injections delay annuitization, alter the structure of the annuitization boundary, and permit positive holdings in risky assets even at zero liquid wealth. Numerical results further reveal that cheaper annuities may increase the expected capital contributions required from the pension sponsor.
item.dc:creator: Yijie Huang, Xiaoqing Liang, Jie Xiong, Xiang Yu

item.title: Finite-horizon Optimal Consumption and Investment with Costly Income Adjustment
item.description: arXiv:2611.03076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study optimal consumption and investment for an investor who receives labor income until a fixed retirement date, can raise the income rate irreversibly at a constant price per unit of income flow, and cannot borrow against future income. A pathwise argument shows that no income is purchased during a final period before retirement whose length depends only on the interest rate and the price. Before this period the dual problem has two free boundaries: a lower one generated by the borrowing constraint and an upper one, at which income is purchased, that escapes to infinity as the final period begins. The analysis of this problem is our main mathematical contribution. During the final period it is a single obstacle problem, which we solve, together with the regularity of its free boundary, by established methods. Before that period a partial hodograph transformation straightens both free boundaries and turns the problem into a quasilinear parabolic equation with oblique boundary conditions on a fixed interval. Comparison principles, explicit barriers and regularity theory for quasilinear equations then give existence, uniqueness and smoothness. Transforming back and gluing the two constructions yields global regularity: both free boundaries are infinitely differentiable and the value function is a classical solution at every positive wealth level. A dual budget process verifies optimality. We also derive coupled Volterra integral equations for the free boundaries, prove exponential convergence to the perpetual problem under a scalar condition, and find numerically a purchase threshold that is U-shaped in the time to retirement.
item.dc:creator: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon

item.title: Partially Active Automated Market Makers
item.description: arXiv:2602.09887v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new class of automated market maker (AMM), the \emph{partially active automated market maker} (PA-AMM). PA-AMM divides its reserves into two parts, the active and the passive parts, and uses only the active part for trading. At the top of every block, such a division is done again to keep the active reserves always being \(\lambda\)-portion of total reserves, where \(\lambda \in (0, 1]\) is an activeness parameter. We show that this simple mechanism reduces adverse selection costs, measured by loss-versus-rebalancing (LVR), and thereby improves the wealth of liquidity providers (LPs) relative to plain constant-function market makers (CFMMs). As a trade-off, the asset weights within a PA-AMM pool may deviate from their target weights implied by its invariant curve. Motivated by the optimal index-tracking problem literature, we also propose and solve an optimization problem that balances such deviation and the reduction of LVR.
item.dc:creator: Sunghun Ko (Eugene), Seungwon (Eugene), Jeong

item.title: Sublinear Markov Semigroups Beyond Uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2609.37881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To what extent does a local operator on smooth test functions determine a sub-Markov semigroup and its underlying structure of laws? Many existing approaches work with Feller semigroups on the space \(C_b\) of bounded continuous functions and rely on uniqueness, often established through a comparison principle for the associated evolution equation. However, even when the local operator is linear, uniqueness may fail and a \(C_b\)-Feller restriction may exclude the associated canonical semigroup. We discover that the space \(\operatorname{USC}_b\) of bounded upper semicontinuous functions offers a natural setting for this study. Within this framework, a complete description of the relationships among sublinear local operators, sublinear sub-Markov semigroups, and their underlying structures of laws is achieved without assuming uniqueness. Under suitable regularity and Lyapunov conditions, we construct the greatest semigroup compatible with a prescribed sublinear local operator and obtain a stochastic representation in terms of a Markov process under sublinear expectations. We characterize all sublinear sub-Markov semigroups dominated by this greatest semigroup in two ways: through a one-to-one correspondence with stable subfamilies of its representing laws, and through an order relation between their infinitesimal generators and the prescribed local operator. We further characterize the greatest semigroup via the greatest viscosity subsolution of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation. These results clarify what information about global stochastic evolution can be recovered from local infinitesimal descriptions and what freedom remains in the absence of uniqueness. The resulting characterizations are new even when the local operator is linear.
item.dc:creator: Jongjin Park, David Criens, Hyungbin Park

item.title: Model Risk Analysis for Entropic Hedging Strategies
item.description: arXiv:2610.06168v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Market incompleteness causes residual profit and loss after hedging that is accounted for with valuation adjustments and bid-offer spreads acting as model risk buffers for the derivative price. Entropic risk optimisation is a general framework for modelling these adjustments. When the prices are quadratic Gaussian, the coupled equations for price and hedge ratios are solved exactly, with a decomposition of the entropic risk into convexity, dimensionality, funding and strategy contributions that are attributed in the explanation of realised P&L. The results are applicable when the underlying prices follow Gaussian processes, such as fractional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. The article concludes with analysis of the continuous hedging limit for these processes, and a discussion of their application in data-driven regressions.
item.dc:creator: Paul McCloud
